full_text_en:
Hainan Tonglian Shipping Co., Ltd. v. Minmetals International Nonferrous Metals Trading Co., Ltd. — retrial of dispute over maritime cargo transport

Retrial Applicant (Appellant at First Instance): Hainan Tonglian Shipping Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Wang Dehu, General Manager

Agent ad litem: Yang Wengui, Attorney at Haitong Law Firm

Retrial Respondent (Appellee at First Instance): Minmetals International Nonferrous Metals Trading Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Zhu Guang, General Manager

Agent ad litem: Qu Xiaogang, Manager of the Company

Agent ad litem: He Xiaorong, Doctoral Candidate at Renmin University of China Law School

In the dispute over maritime cargo transport between Hainan Tonglian Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tonglian Company) and Minmetals International Nonferrous Metals Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Minmetals Company), the Hainan High People's Court rendered a final civil judgment on December 31, 1996. Tonglian Company, dissatisfied with that final judgment, filed a petition with the Supreme People's Court, requesting a retrial. The Supreme People's Court decided to bring the case up for trial.

The Supreme People's Court, upon retrial, finds the following facts:

On November 20, 1995, Minmetals Company and Toyota Tsusho Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Toyota Tsusho) entered into a sales contract for 1,500 metric tons of low-phosphorus silicon-manganese alloy. Subsequently, the parties agreed that the actual quantity to be performed would be 1,200 metric tons. The export agent for Minmetals Company was Hainan International Trade Center (hereinafter referred to as Hainan International Trade). To transport these 1,200 metric tons of goods, Hainan International Trade, on December 11, 1995, entered into a voyage charter party with Guangdong Zhanjiang Haitong Shipping Agency Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haitong Company) on behalf of Minmetals Company. Haitong Company then entered into another voyage charter party with China Ocean Shipping Agency Guangdong Zhanjiang Company (hereinafter referred to as Zhanjiang Sinotrans). Zhanjiang Sinotrans, in turn, entered into a charter party with Dalian Wufeng Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Wufeng Company). The terms of these three linked contracts were substantially identical, all agreeing to charter the vessel "Wansheng" to transport the 1,200 metric tons of goods involved in this case. The registered owner of the vessel "Wansheng" was Tonglian Company. The vessel was actually placed under the operation and management of Dalian Gangwantong Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Gangwantong Company), which also provided the crew. Gangwantong Company further chartered the vessel to Wufeng Company on a time charter basis.

On December 25, 1995, Minmetals Company's 1,200 metric tons of low-phosphorus silicon-manganese alloy were loaded onto the "Wansheng," under Bill of Lading No. HX-95B, with the destination port being Nagoya, Japan. On the same voyage, the "Wansheng" also carried another shipment of 1,200 metric tons of high-phosphorus silicon-manganese alloy destined for Kawasaki, Japan. The external appearance of both shipments was identical. On December 27, 1995, the "Wansheng" departed from Haikou Port and arrived at Nagoya Port, Japan, on January 8, 1996. During unloading, the vessel misdischarged the two shipments. On January 26, 1996, Toyota Tsusho demanded compensation from Minmetals Company on the grounds that the goods did not conform to the contract requirements. Minmetals Company made an ex gratia payment to Toyota Tsusho. Due to the impact of the performance of this contract, a subsequent sales contract for silicon-manganese alloy between Minmetals Company and Toyota Tsusho could not be smoothly performed, causing losses to Minmetals Company.

It was further found that Bill of Lading No. HX-95B for the 1,200 metric tons of low-phosphorus silicon-manganese alloy had been endorsed and transferred twice. Toyota Tsusho, the buyer under the sales contract, had taken delivery of the goods at the destination port of Nagoya and had disposed of the shipment.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including the import-export goods sales contract, charter parties, and trial transcripts.

Minmetals Company filed a claim for compensation against Tonglian Company. After Tonglian Company refused to compensate, Minmetals Company instituted an action against Tonglian Company in the Haikou Maritime Court, requesting a judgment ordering Tonglian Company to compensate it for losses of USD 610,000 and to bear the litigation costs. The Haikou Maritime Court, after trial, held that this was a dispute over a maritime cargo transport contract, that the legal relationship of a transport contract between Minmetals Company and Tonglian Company was established, and that Tonglian Company, as the carrier under the transport contract, should bear civil liability for the misdischarge. The court ruled that Tonglian Company compensate Minmetals Company for economic losses of USD 461,000 and RMB 81,000, and dismissed Minmetals Company's other claims. The first-instance case acceptance fee was to be borne by Minmetals Company in the amount of RMB 10,000 and by Tonglian Company in the amount of RMB 30,000.

Tonglian Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment of the Haikou Maritime Court, appealed to the Hainan High People's Court on the grounds that Minmetals Company lacked standing to sue, that Tonglian Company should not be the defendant in this case, that it was not at fault for the misdischarge, that the facts found by the first-instance court were unclear, and that the law was incorrectly applied.

The Hainan High People's Court, after trial, held that Minmetals Company was the shipper named on the bill of lading and the party that physically delivered the goods, and therefore had the right, in its capacity as shipper, to bring an action against the carrier under the maritime cargo transport contract for the erroneous delivery of the goods. Tonglian Company, as the actual carrier, should bear liability for compensating Minmetals Company for the losses caused by its erroneous delivery. The court accordingly dismissed the appeal and affirmed the original judgment. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 40,000 was to be borne by Tonglian Company.

Tonglian Company, dissatisfied with the final judgment of the Hainan High People's Court, filed a retrial application with the Supreme People's Court. Its grounds were: after the transfer of the bill of lading, Minmetals Company, as the shipper, no longer had any interest in the goods and lacked standing to sue; in the voyage transport involved in this case, Tonglian Company was merely the registered owner of the "Wansheng," which was actually operated and managed by Gangwantong Company, and Tonglian Company's status was equivalent to that of a bareboat charterer; and in this voyage, Tonglian Company had no fault whatsoever and should not be the defendant in this case.

Minmetals Company replied: Minmetals Company was a directly interested party in this case and had complete standing as plaintiff; Tonglian Company's act of misdischarge directly infringed upon Minmetals Company's civil rights and interests; Tonglian Company, as the actual carrier, should bear full legal liability for its wrongful act of misdischarge and should be liable for all economic losses caused to Minmetals Company by its wrongful act; Minmetals Company bore no fault whatsoever for Tonglian Company's act of misdischarge.

The Supreme People's Court held: This case is a dispute over a maritime cargo transport contract. To export its 1,200 metric tons of low-phosphorus silicon-manganese alloy, Minmetals Company's export agent, Hainan International Trade, entered into a voyage charter party with Haitong Company. Subsequently, Haitong Company entered into a linked voyage charter party with Zhanjiang Sinotrans, and Zhanjiang Sinotrans entered into another linked voyage charter party with Wufeng Company. The vessel chartered under all these linked charter parties was the "Wansheng," of which Tonglian Company was the registered owner. During the relevant voyage, the vessel had been placed under the operation and management of Gangwantong Company, and the crew were also provided by Gangwantong Company. The Bill of Lading No. HX-95B involved in this case was also issued by Gangwantong Company. During the relevant voyage, the vessel was operated under a time charter by Wufeng Company. Minmetals Company had neither a transport contract relationship evidenced by a bill of lading nor a charter party relationship with Tonglian Company. Therefore, Minmetals Company, as the shipper under the bill of lading, had no contractual basis to sue Tonglian Company.

Maritime cargo transport is a common link in international trade. According to the terms of the sales contract, one party is responsible for booking shipping space. The seller, as the owner of the goods, delivers the goods to the carrier at the port of loading. The carrier then issues a bill of lading to the seller, who uses the bill of lading to settle payment under the payment terms of the sales contract. The buyer, after paying for the documents, becomes the lawful holder of the bill of lading. At the port of destination, the buyer presents the bill of lading to the carrier to take delivery of the goods and becomes the owner of the goods under the bill of lading, thereby concluding the international trade cargo flow process. In this case, Minmetals Company, as the seller under the sales contract and the shipper under the bill of lading, had ownership of the 1,200 metric tons of low-phosphorus silicon-manganese alloy under Bill of Lading No. HX-95B at the time of issuance of the bill of lading. However, after the bill of lading was endorsed and transferred twice to Toyota Tsusho, the buyer under the sales contract, and after Toyota Tsusho took delivery of the goods at Nagoya Port, Japan, the transport contract had completed the procedures for delivery and receipt of goods at the port of destination. The bill of lading had circulated normally. At this point, the rights and obligations of the shipper under the transport contract evidenced by the bill of lading had been transferred to Toyota Tsusho, the holder of the bill of lading, including the ownership of the goods under the bill of lading and the right of action. Therefore, Minmetals Company, as the shipper under the bill of lading, no longer had a substantive right of claim over the goods under the bill of lading. Minmetals Company no longer had a legal interest in the matter vis-à-vis the carrier. The right to claim damages for the loss caused by the misdischarge of goods by the "Wansheng" should be exercised by Toyota Tsusho. Toyota Tsusho had the option, according to the terms of the sales contract, to claim compensation for damages from the seller of the goods, Minmetals Company, or, according to the cargo transport contract, to claim compensation for damages from the carrier under the bill of lading. Toyota Tsusho chose to claim compensation from the seller of the goods, Minmetals Company, according to the terms of the sales contract. That was Toyota Tsusho's right. However, under the circumstances where Minmetals Company made an ex gratia payment to Toyota Tsusho and Toyota Tsusho did not assign to Minmetals Company its right to claim against the carrier under the transport contract evidenced by the bill of lading, Minmetals Company no longer had any rights over the goods under the bill of lading. Minmetals Company did not automatically acquire a right of recourse against the carrier under the bill of lading. Therefore, Minmetals Company, as shipper, has no legal basis to sue Tonglian Company for damages to the goods under the bill of lading and does not have standing to sue Tonglian Company. Tonglian Company's retrial application is meritorious and should be upheld. Upon discussion by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, and pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item 2, Article 184, paragraph 1, and Article 108 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ordered as follows:

1. The civil judgment (1996) Qiong Jing Zhong Zi No. 137 of the Hainan High People's Court is hereby reversed;
2. The civil judgment (1996) Hai Shang Chu Zi No. 037 of the Haikou Maritime Court is hereby reversed;
3. The lawsuit filed by Minmetals Company is dismissed.

The first-instance and second-instance litigation costs, each in the amount of RMB 40,000, shall be borne by Minmetals Company.
